meta.title: Are more users new, retained or returning?
meta.question: Which group is largest each month?
meta.author: Codex

items: Each numbered check refers to a SQL evidence log.
Counts are distinct identified active users within each month.
New
Active and signed up in the month.
Retained
Active in this month and the previous month.
Returning
Active this month, not the previous month, and signed up earlier; called resurrected in the registry.

blocks.text: Retained users are the largest group in every month from May to September 2026. In September, 5,071 (44.3%) were retained, 4,656 (40.7%) returning, and 1,720 (15.0%) new. (Checks 4 and 6)

blocks.title: Coverage
blocks.text: Unidentified sessions are excluded. September had 3,703 such sessions, whose distinct users and categories are unknown. (Checks 5 and 10)

items: Growth accounting v1.0 and MAU v1.1; UTC months use inclusive start, exclusive next-month start. April lacks a growth row because March is outside the coverage window.
Gold was reconciled at build and independently recounted from Silver for September.
Checked database inventory, metadata, build, monthly results, Silver recount, identity coverage and quality.
The comparison directly answers the question; no causal hypotheses were tested.
Percentages use the same month’s identified MAU; rounding may affect totals. Do not sum distinct users across months. (Check 4)
September MAU rose by 576 from August: 1,720 new + 4,656 returning − 5,800 churned = 576. Churned means active in August but not September. (Check 4)
Of September returning users, 157 had their first observed session in September despite earlier signup. (Check 6)
No cause is established by these counts.
September’s 3,703 unidentified sessions include one beginning in August. Session counts are not people; unknown identities could affect the retained–returning gap of 415. (Checks 5 and 10)

September Silver recount matches Gold. No missing profiles, future signups, duplicate or null user-day keys, flagged activity rows or flagged profiles were found. Thirteen payment corrections are outside this activity metric. (Checks 6, 7, 9)

Build succeeded and reports passing growth and MAU reconciliation. Current registry hash differs from the build registry hash; same metric versions and the September recount support this result, but full registry equivalence and source freshness were not independently established. (Check 3)
Returning includes people first active after signup month, including those signed up before coverage.
Metadata snapshot and synthetic completeness are assertions, not a verified database hash or proof of real-world telemetry completeness.

First five checks were logged before the snapshot was known; check 2 records its value. Repository has no Git metadata: local directory timestamp 2026-11-09 20:12:48 IST is a copy-date proxy, not a verified download date.
Track buckets and identity coverage together; improve linkage before extrapolating to all visitors.
If only previously active reactivations should count as returning, agree the definition and recompute.
